direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature is a context‐switch or “query‐response” signal. When active it indicates that the preceding text is a user question (or similar prompt), so the model should transition into a proper, well–segmented answer. direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature “lights up” exactly when the model is processing a word‐piece that is an incomplete (or leading) portion of a word—that is, it signals that the current token is a subword prefix that needs to be “completed” by the following token. In short, it encodes a word‐fragment or subword‐continuation signal.

results.text: The feature activates when it processes a token like 'ex' that stands for the beginning of 'example'.
When encountering the subword prefix 'un' as part of 'unlikely', the indicator lights up to signal continuation.
An incomplete fragment such as 'pre' in 'preview' triggers the feature since it marks the start of a multi-token word.
The feature signals upon detecting a token fragment like 'mis' at the beginning of 'misinterpretation'.
When a word-piece like 'inter' appears as a leading fragment before being completed in 'interaction', the light goes on.
The activation occurs when processing 'sub' in 'submarine' as it indicates that more tokens need to complete the word.
A token such as 'auto' in 'automobile', recognized as an incomplete part, triggers the feature immediately.
The feature lights up upon seeing a partial token like 'trans' which signals that additional characters will follow to form 'transport'.
When a subword prefix like 'bio' is processed as part of 'biology', the system registers it as an incomplete token.
The incomplete token fragment 'anti' in 'antibody' activates the feature, indicating a pending continuation.
The feature remains inactive when processing a complete word like 'apple' that does not need continuation.
A full token such as 'orange' does not trigger the light because it stands alone without being a subword prefix.
When handling a complete word like 'dog', the feature does not activate as there is no fragment to complete.
The indicator does not light up for a complete token like 'cat', which is processed in its entirety.
For whole words like 'banana', the feature does not recognize any subword continuation signal.
A punctuation mark like '.', processed as a complete symbol, does not cause the feature to light up.
Processing a full token such as 'quick' does not trigger the subword signal since it requires no additional fragment.
When a complete word like 'brown' is processed, the system does not register it as needing further tokens.
The feature remains off for standalone complete tokens like 'fox' that are not split into subword fragments.
A complete token such as 'jumps' does not trigger the feature because it is not an incomplete subword that needs to join with another token.

direction_summaries.explanation: It appears that this feature is a context‐switch or “query‐response” signal. When active it indicates that the preceding text is a user question (or similar prompt), so the model should transition into a proper, well–segmented answer. In its absence the predicted continuation becomes a garbled fragment (e.g. “cknowled”) because the model loses that cue for the correct answer–initiation token boundary.

Assistant: The current President is [Name].
